header.Title (Source): King Arthur - Sword in the Stone

text.S1: LONG, long ago, after Uther Pendragon died, there was no King in Britain, and every Knight hoped to seize the crown for himself. The country was likely to fare ill when laws were broken on every side, and the corn which was to give the poor bread was trodden underfoot, and there was none to bring the evildoer to justice.
text.S2: A very long time ago, after the death of Uther Pendragon no King ruled Britain, therefore, every Knight hoped to seize the crown for himself. In that regard, there would be confusion in case laws were not regarded with impunity, and the corn which was to give the poor bread was trodden underfoot as there would be no justice because culprits would go unpunished..
text.T1: KALE-kale koo, kasamulaho wa lifu la Uther Pendragon kwaina kusina Mulena mwa naha ya Britain, mi yanaa filwe mushukwe wa bundwalume kaufela naa hupula kuipa mushukwe wa bulena ili yena. Kacwalo, naha neika sinyeha milao hane ika lobiwa mwa maneku kaufela, mi bubeke bobuciwa bone bulukelwa kufa babotana sico nebuka hatakiwa mi hakuna yanaa kafitisa lifosi kwamulawo.
text.T2: Kwa kale kale koo, kasamulaho wa lifu la Uther Pendragon kwaina kusina Mulena mwa naha ya Britain, mi yanaa filwe mushukwe wa bundwalume kaufela naa hupula kuipamushukwe wa bulena ili yena. Kacwalo, naha neika sinyeha milao hane ika lobiwa mwa maneku kaufela, mi bubeke bobuciwa bone bulukelwa kufa babotana sico nebuka hatakiwami hakuna yanaa kafitisa lifosi kwa mulawo.

text.S1: Then, when things were at their worst, came forth Merlin the magician, and fast he rode to the place where the Archbishop of Canterbury had his dwelling. And they took counsel together, and agreed that all the lords and gentlemen of Britain should ride to London and meet on Christmas Day, now at hand, in the Great Church. So this was done. And on Christmas morning, as they left the church, they saw in the church yard a large stone, and on it a bar of steel, and in the steel a naked sword was held, and about it was written in letters of gold, ‘Whoso pulleth out this sword is by right of birth King of England.’
text.S2: It was experienced that when there was no control, came a magician called Merlin who visited the Archbishop of Canterbury’s residence. They counseled each other and agreed that in Britain, all the lords and gentlemen should ride to London and meet on Christmas Day in the Great Church. That was achieved. Then in the morning of Christmas Day, after they had left the Church they saw a rock which was located around the Church yard. On the rock was a steel bar and a naked sword was held in the steel where letters of gold were written about the naked sword, “Whoso pulleth out this sword is by right of birth King of England.”
text.T1: Cwale lika hase lisinyehile hahulu, kwataha mutu wa mabibo yabizwa Merlin mi kapili-pili aya kwa muyaho wanaa pila Mumbishopu yomuhulu wa mwa Canterbury. Bayo elezana ni kulumelelana hamoho kuli Malena kaufela ba naha ya Britain baye kwa tolopo ya London kuli bayo kopanela-teñi ka lizazi la Kilisimasi, mwa Keleke yetuna. Kwaezahala cwalo. Kacwalo, kakusasana ka lizazi la Kilisimasi hase basiile Keleke, babona licwe-tuna lene lifumaneha mwa lapa la Keleke. Mwa licwe lewo neku coñilwe sipi, mi fa sipi yewo nekuna ni mukwale ili fone kuñozwi litaku za gauda sina cwana, “Mutu ukona kucomola mukwale wo ka tukelo ya sipepo sa Mulena wa naha ya England.”

text.S1: They marveled at these words, and called for the Archbishop, and brought him into the place where the stone stood. Then those Knights who fain would be King could not hold themselves back, and they tugged at the sword with all their might; but it never stirred. The Archbishop watched them in silence, but when they were faint from pulling he spoke: ‘The man is not here who shall lift out that sword, nor do I know where to find him. But this is my counsel that two Knights be chosen, good and true men, to keep guard over the sword.’
text.S2: What surprised them most were those words. Therefore, they invited the Archbishop into the palace to come and see the site of the stone. Then those who were knighted and wished to be were not ready to hold back and struggled to remove the sword out but failed. As they were doing that, the Archbishop watched them in silence. And when their attempts to pull it out was in vain he said, “The man is not here who shall lift out that sword, nor do I know where to find him. But this is my counsel that two Knights be chosen, good and true men, to keep guard over the sword.”
text.T1: Bakomokiswa hahulu ki manzwi awo mi bamema Mumbishopu yomutuna kuli atahe kwa Kwandu ato iponela sene sili fone liyemi licwe. Cwale bawo bane bafilwe mishukwe ya bundwalume yakuli batabela kuba Mulena neba sike bakutela mwamulaho mi balika kucomola mukwale ka maata kono neu sika nyangana ni kamuta. Mumbishopu yomutuna aba talima inge akuzize feela, Cwale hase bapalezwi kucomola mukwale ali, “Haayo fa muuna yalukela kucomola mukwale woo. Hape na hani zibi koni kona kumu fumana. Ki yona kelezo yaaka ye, yakuli kuketiwe bababeli babafilwe mishukwe ya bundwalume, ili bangana baana baniti, kuli balibelele mukwale.”

text.S1: Thus it was done. But the lords and gentlemen-at-arms cried out that every man had a right to try to win the sword, and they decided that on New Year’s Day a tournament should be held, and any Knight who would, might enter the lists.
text.S2: In that regard, it was successful. However, the Lords and the Security Guards yelled that every man had a right to try to win the sword. Therefore, they planned that on New Year’s Day they should hold a tournament so that interested Knight would be enlisted in the competition.
text.T1: Kwaezwa cwalo. Kono Malena ni baana babalibeleli bahuwa bali ki tukelo ya muuna kaufela ya kuli alike kutula kuli aange mukwale. Kamukwawocwalo, balela kuli ka lizazi la Nyuyele kube ni papali ya kangisano kuli yafilwe mushukwe wa bundwalume yatabela kaufela ai ñolise.

text.S1: So on New Year’s Day, the Knights, as their custom was, went to hear service in the Great Church, and after it was over they met in the field to make ready for the tourney. Among them was a brave Knight called Sir Ector, who brought with him Sir Kay, his son, and Arthur, Kay’s foster-brother. Now Kay had unbuckled his sword the evening before, and in his haste to be at the tourney had forgotten to put it on again, and he begged Arthur to ride back and fetch it for him. But when Arthur reached the house the door was locked, for the women had gone out to see the tourney, and though Arthur tried his best to get in he could not.
text.S2: It happened that on New Year’s Day all knights, as per their tradition attended service in Great Church. After the Church Service, they then convened at the playing field to prepare for the competition. One of them was a brave Knight called Sir Ector who was accompanied by his son called sir. Kay together with Kay’s foster-brother. Then Kay had unpacked his sword the evening before, unfortunately, because of being in a hurry, he had forgotten to repack it and he begged Arthur to travel back and fetch it for him. Unfortunately, when Arthur arrived at the house the door was locked because the women had gone to watch the tournament as a result he tried hard to enter the house but in vain.

Sebelezo hase ifelile, bakopanela mwa mutabo ka kui tukiseza lipapali za likanganisano. Halaa bona neeli wa mushukwe wa bundume yanaa bizwa Sir. Ector, yanaa tile ni mwanaahae Sir. Kay, hamoho cwalo ni Arthur, muzwale wa Kay yanaa añulwa ni yena. Cwanoñu, Kay naase atamuluzi kale mukwale wahae manzibuana a lizazi lelifelile. Cwale ka ñalelwa ya kunyangufela kwa lipapali za likanganisano alibala kutama mukwale wahae hape mi ki haa kupa Arthur kukutela kwa hae fa pelesa kuyo mubatela wona. text.S1: Then he rode away in great anger, and said to himself, ‘Kay shall not be without a sword this day. I will take that sword in the churchyard, and give it to him’; and he galloped fast till he reached the gate of the churchyard. Here he jumped down and tied his horse tightly to a tree, then, running up to the stone, he seized the handle of the sword, and drew it easily out; afterwards he mounted his horse again, and delivered the sword to Sir Kay. The moment Sir Kay saw the sword he knew it was not his own, but the sword of the stone, and he sought out his father Sir Ector, and said to him, ‘Sir, this is the sword of the stone, therefore I am the rightful King.’
text.S2: Therefore, he returned to the tournament venue annoyed and said to himself, ‘Kay shall not be without a sword this day. I will take that sword in the churchyard, and give it to him.’ He galloped the horse fast till he reached the entrance of the churchyard. He jumped down and tied his horse tightly to a tree. Then, he ran up to the rock, he seized the handle of the sword, and pulled it out easily; afterwards he mounted his horse again, and delivered the sword to Sir Kay. Immediately Sir Kay had noticed the sword he knew it was not his own sword, but of the stone. He then sought out his father Sir Ector, and said to him, ‘Sir, this is the sword of the stone, therefore I am the rightful King.’

text.S1: Sir Ector made no answer, but signed to Kay and Arthur to follow him, and they all three went back to the church. Leaving their horses outside, they entered the choir, and here Sir Ector took a holy book and bade Sir Kay swear how he came by that sword. ‘My brother Arthur gave it to me,’ replied Sir Kay. ‘How did you come by it?’ asked Sir Ector, turning to Arthur. ‘Sir,’ said Arthur, ‘when I rode home for my brother’s sword I found no one to deliver it to me, and as I resolved he should not be sword less I thought of the sword in this stone, and I pulled it out.’ ‘Were any Knights present when you did this?’ asked Sir Ector. ‘No, none,’ said Arthur. ‘Then it is you,’ said Sir Ector, ‘who are the rightful King of this land.’
text.S2: Sir Ector did not reply to him but only used sign language to Kay and Arthur to follow him. Therefore, the three of them went back to church. text.S1: ‘But why am I the King?’ inquired Arthur. ‘Because,’ answered Sir Ector, ‘this is an enchanted sword, and no man could draw it but he who was born a King. Therefore put the sword back into the stone, and let me see you take it out.’ ‘That is soon done,’ said Arthur, replacing the sword, and Sir Ector himself tried to draw it, but he could not. ‘Now it is your turn,’ he said to Sir Kay, but Sir Kay fared no better than his father, though he tugged with all his might and main. ‘Now you, Arthur,’ and Arthur pulled it out as easily as if it had been lying in its sheath, and as he did so Sir Ector and Sir Kay sank on their knees before him.
text.S2: “But why am I the King?” asked Arthur. “Because,” replied Sir Ector, “this is an enchanted sword, and no man could draw it but he who was born a King. text.S1: ‘Why do you, my father and brother, kneel to me?’ asked Arthur in surprise. ‘Nay, nay, my lord,’ answered Sir Ector, ‘I was never your father, though till to-day I did not know who your father really was. You are the son of Uther Pendragon, and you were brought to me when you were born by Merlin himself, who promised that when the time came I should know from whom you sprang. And now it has been revealed to me.’ But when Arthur heard that Sir Ector was not his father, he wept bitterly. ‘If I am King,’ he said at last, ‘ask what you will, and I shall not fail you. For to you, and to my lady and mother, I owe more than to anyone in the world, for she loved me and treated me as her son.’ ‘Sir,’ replied Sir Ector, ‘I only ask that you make your foster-brother, Sir Kay, Seneschal¹ of all your lands.’ ‘That I will readily,’ answered Arthur, ‘and while he and I live no other shall fill that once.’

text.S1: Sir Ector then made them seek out the Archbishop with him, and they told him all that had happened concerning the sword, which Arthur had left standing in the stone. And on the Twelfth Day the Knights and Barons came again, but none could draw it out but Arthur. When they saw this, many of the Barons became angry and cried out that they would never own a boy for a King whose blood was no better than their own. So it was agreed to wait till Candlemas, when more Knights might be there, and meanwhile the same two men who had been chosen before watched the sword night and day; but at Candlemas it was the same thing, and at Easter. And when Pentecost came, the common people who were present, and saw Arthur pull out the sword, cried with one voice that he was their King, and they would kill any man who said differently. Then all around fell on their knees before him, and Arthur took the sword and offered it upon the altar where the Archbishop stood, and the best man that was there made him Knight. After that the crown was put on his head, and he swore to his lords and commons that he would be a true King and would do them justice all the days of his life.
text.S2: After that had happened, Sir Ector asked them to seek out the Archbishop with him, so they informed him of all that had happened concerning the sword which Arthur had left standing in the rock. Still more, on the Twelfth Day the Knights and Barons came again to attempt to draw it out but none of them could but Arthur. When they saw this, many of the Barons became angry and cried out that they would never foster a boy for a King whose blood was no better than their own. After that the crown was put on his head, and he swore to his lords and commons that he would be a truthful King and would do them justice throughout his life time.
text.T1: Kasamulaho a zewo, Sir Ector cwale aba laela kuli hamoho ni yena babonane ni Mumbishopu yomutuna kuli atalusezwe sesi ezahalile kaufela kuama taba ya mukwale woo Arthur nasiile inge ucomekilwe mwa licwe. Kacwalo, mwa lizazi la butwelufu, Bamishukwe ya bundwalme ni Baeteleli bataha hape kono bapalelwa kucomola mukwale mwa licwe konji Arthur. Hase baboni cwalo buñata bwa Baeteleli bafilikana ni kuhuwaka kuli habana kuluwa mushimani kuli abe Mulena yoo mali a mwa mubili wahae naa saswani kwa butuna ni abona. Cwale he balumelelana kuli balibelele kufitela lizazi la mukiti wa kupuzo ya Kresite wokabela mwa Tempele, ili foo bamishukwe ya bundwalume babañata bakabelateñi. Hape nicwalo, baana bababeli bane bakile baketiwa kumamela mukwale busihu ni musihali nebaliteñi, Hape nto yeswana nei ezahezi lizazi la mukiti wa kupuzo ya Kresite wa mwa Tempele, mane ni fa lizazi la Paseka. Cwale lizazi la Pentekonta halifita, batu feela bane baliteñi bane baboni Arthur inge acomola mukwale mwa licwe, bahuwa ka muhuwo ulimuñwi kuli neeli Mulenaabona mi nebaka bulaya mutu ya naana ni mubulelelo usili. Cwale kaufelaabona bamu kubamela ka mañwele abona fapilaahae. Haili yena Arthur aanga mukwale ni kuwiisa kwa katala kwanaa yemi Mumbishopu yomutuna mi muuna wangana yanaali-teñi afiwa mushukwe.wa bundwalume kasamulaho abeiwa ni mushukwe wa bulena kwa toho ni kui konka ka luci fapilaa Malena ni batu feela kuli ukaba Mulena waniti ni kubafa liswanelo zabona mwa mazazi a bupilo bwahae kaufela.
